page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 2 physical cores and 1 thread per core, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.r6.large sits in the lower performance tiers for compute and memory throughput. In stress-ng testing, single-core performance reached 1298.79, while multi-core performance scored 1726.78, placing it in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested instances. Memory bandwidth tests show 96.46 GB/sec for cached small blocks and drop to 13.08 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Passmark CPU and memory scores are 2133.1 and 1618.31, respectively. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also modest, with Redis achieving 1.67 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r6.large offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring a larger memory footprint relative to compute resources. Because it pairs 16.0 GB of RAM with only 2 vCPUs, it avoids the expense of paying for unneeded compute cores. However, the tradeoff is limited processing power and lower memory bandwidth. This makes the instance suitable for lightweight database caching, small-scale Redis deployments, basic web serving, and memory-bound utility workloads that do not demand high CPU throughput.
